title: Numeric representation assumptions escaped their valid domain
summary: Three promoted engineering records now support a provisional cross-case pattern: an engineered system represented a physical quantity through units, numeric range, or time precision under assumptions that stopped being valid at an interface, mission envelope, or uptime boundary. The pattern is deliberately not final; it is an earned candidate awaiting negative controls and more cases.

status_history.note: Interface ambiguity / units mismatch recurrence existed as a quarantined seed pattern.
Promoted above seed-only because three official-report-backed records now support a bounded provisional pattern.
Air Canada Flight 143 / Gimli Glider added as a positive-control record; pattern remains candidate and still needs negative controls and caught-before-harm counterexamples.

claims.claim: MCO, Ariane 5 Flight 501, and the Dhahran Patriot failure each contain an official-source-backed pathway in which numeric representation assumptions crossed a boundary where they no longer held.
what_would_change_status: A second review finds one case's official causal claim has been overstated.
Negative controls show that the proposed pattern is too broad to explain recurrence.
A better pattern label separates unit-interface failures, range-overflow failures, and time-precision failures into distinct families.

limitations: Three cases are enough to preserve a candidate pattern, not enough to claim frequency or causal law.
No negative controls have been added.
The pattern may need to split into subpatterns: units, numeric range, and time precision.
evidence_profile.red_team_state: rev0017 adds first positive control; negative controls and caught-before-harm counterexamples still missing

type_payload.short_definition: A physical or operational quantity is encoded under assumptions about units, numeric range, precision, or validity window; the encoded value then crosses a boundary where the assumption is false, and surrounding checks/tests fail to catch it.

case_evidence.mechanism: Required metric impulse units but ground output used English-force units; downstream model consumed wrong scale.
A reused alignment computation produced a horizontal-velocity-related value outside the assumed range in Ariane 5's trajectory.
Internal-clock time conversion lost precision after extended uptime, shifting the predicted detection window.

not_this: Not every software failure is a numeric-assumption failure.
Not every numeric bug is an engineering-disaster pattern.
The pattern does not by itself establish blame or preventability without case-specific source support.
needed_before_synthesis: Add at least two more cases and at least two negative controls.
Split or merge subpatterns after comparing with unit-conversion, overflow, precision-loss, and stale-assumption cases.
Add test-design fields: what simulation/test would have exposed the invalid assumption?

positive_controls_needed: At least one caught-before-harm unit/range/precision control case is still needed; Gimli is a positive control but not a prevention success.
negative_controls_needed: Add software or engineering incidents with serious outcomes where numeric representation was present but not explanatory, to prevent the pattern from absorbing all technical failure.
counterexamples_to_seek: A case with unit/range/precision mismatch caught by interface tests before harm; this would help define prevention boundaries.
rollback_triggers: A second-review extraction demotes or materially weakens one of the support records.
A negative-control record shows the pattern label fits too many unrelated cases.
A counterexample shows the claimed recurrence is better explained by a narrower or different mechanism.
The pattern is upgraded only after controls and not by record count alone.
red_team_controls.split_or_merge_watch: High: unit-conversion, integer range, floating precision, stale clock, and reused-envelope assumptions may deserve separate subpatterns.

maturity_gate.minimum_before_mature: At least one positive control, at least one negative control, an explicit counterexample search, and a rollback/split decision recorded in the claim-status ledger.
